chunks: Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon him.
Indeed, ʿAli, peace be upon him, would not validate the testimony of one man based on the testimony of another man, except the testimony of two men based on the testimony of one man.

key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a male witness in the legal context
key_terms.عَلَى: based upon or concerning, in the context of testimony upon testimony
key_terms.لَا يُجِيزُ: he did not validate or deem acceptable

ai.seo_question: When is testimony based on another person’s testimony accepted in Islamic legal rulings?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling from Imam ʿAli عليه السلام concerning testimony based on testimony. It indicates that the testimony of a single man transmitting another man’s testimony is not accepted, unless two men testify to that testimony, reflecting caution and rigor in judicial proof.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3352 - Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):
"Indeed, Imam Ali (as) would not validate the testimony of one man based on the testimony of another man, except if there were two men testifying based on testimony of one man."
